Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to approval on the Dedicated reserve but procurement needs formal language on the throughput guarantee and how you will measure tokens/sec and latency in our Dedicated pool. Specifically:

- Do you guarantee sustained tokens/sec and/or requests/sec for the committed GPU pool, and how is tokens/sec defined (input tokens, output tokens, or both)?
- What latency targets will you guarantee at the commit level (p95, p99) — is that first-token latency or end-to-end?
- What is your measurement methodology (synthetic harness, replay of production traces, warm-up procedures, measurement windows)?
- If the service misses the guarantee, what credits/financial remedies do you provide, and how are edge cases (bursts, autoscaling time) handled?

We have a quarterly internal bar for production readiness and need these answers to align procurement language. Can you send a decision log we can attach to the SOW?

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Dedicated commit — throughput guarantees and measurement

Ashley — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise decision log and proposed acceptance method we can include in the SOW. I copied Aditya and Marissa for technical and commercial details.

Summary decisions (proposal):
- Guaranteed metric: sustained tokens/sec measured as combined input+output tokens (server-side tokenization) across the committed GPU pool. We will also report requests/sec as a secondary metric for correlation.
- Measurement window: a rolling 30-minute stable window is used to determine sustained tokens/sec. A sustained window requires that token production does not drop below 95% of measured value for more than 90 seconds.
- Latency targets: p95 First-Token latency <= 450ms; p95 End-to-End response latency <= 1500ms for responses <= 1,000 tokens. Per-token p99 <= 20ms.
- Acceptance run: a 3-hour acceptance window run in your Dedicated environment (customer-owned VPC) combining a recorded production trace and a synthetic tail-heavy workload. Warm-up: 20 minutes to prime KV caches.
- Remedies: service credit equal to 3x hourly prorated commit value for each hourly shortfall bucket, up to 30% of monthly fee; escalation path to technical review and remediation. Re-runs allowed if customer provides logs within 48h.
- Edge handling: Burst protection and autoscaling cooldowns are excluded from sustained-window calculation; failures attributable to customer networking or misconfigurations are excluded.

I'll let Aditya add the technical harness details and Marissa will outline how credits map to discount bands. If that looks good we'll formalize as a Decision Log entry for the SOW.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding the technical acceptance plan and measurement specifics so procurement has something concrete to reference. Key points:

1) Token definition: we measure server-side tokenization using the BPE vocab associated with the serving model (rwd-base-30B-q4 in the quoted config). The guaranteed metric is the sum of input tokens + generated tokens as observed at the serving runtime, aggregated per request.

2) Measurement harness:
   - We provide a Dockerized harness that replays either (a) a customer-supplied production trace (recommended) or (b) our synthetic tail-heavy workload (we'll supply the trace generator).
   - The harness respects realistic pacing and simulates client-side concurrency to match target RPS distribution.
   - Warm-up: 20 minutes (no measurements during warm-up).

3) Stable-window algorithm (rolled out into runbook):
   - Slide a 30-minute window across the 3-hour run. For each window compute total tokens produced ÷ window seconds = tokens/sec. Report the maximum sustained tokens/sec across windows that meet the stability constraint (no >5% drop for more than 90s).

4) Latency measurement:
   - First-token latency measured at server egress (time from request receive to first byte on the wire). p95 threshold <= 450ms.
   - End-to-end latency measured as time to last byte; p95 <= 1500ms for responses <= 1,000 tokens. For longer responses we use normalized per-token p99 <= 20ms.

5) Measurement environment & priming:
   - Tests run in the customer's Dedicated pool with production network routing. We will coordinate a maintenance window for the acceptance run.
   - KV cache priming is required (20-minute warm-up of representative prompt set).

6) Failure attribution and re-runs:
   - If we observe infra-level anomalies (hardware, driver faults, or our runtime errors) we will accept the failure and provide remediation/credits. If customer networking or misconfigurations are implicated, we will exclude that run and propose a re-run once resolved.

7) Scripts & reproducibility:
   - We will check in the exact harness scripts and raw logs to the shared Drive link and produce an artifact (CSV) listing per-window tokens/sec and latency distribution.

I'll attach the detailed runbook and reference scripts.

— Aditya

Redwood Inference

Ashley — commercial mapping for the decision items above:

- Commit bands: we have three bands: Silver (baseline), Gold (+15% tokens/sec, 8% discount), Platinum (+30% tokens/sec, 15% discount). Discounts apply to committed monthly spend only.
- Credits: If sustained tokens/sec for the month falls below the contracted band by more than 10% in an invoice period, we apply credits as follows: 1-4% shortfall = 5% monthly credit; 4-10% = 10% monthly credit; >10% = 20% monthly credit capped at 30% of the invoice. Credits are calculated after exception handling described in the runbook.
- Downtier: If performance shortfall >20% for 3 consecutive months (after excluding justified events), we reserve the right to re-evaluate the committed band and adjust pricing or recommend increased commit.

We can bake the exact formulas into the SOW. For this deal I will propose Gold band commitment with the 8% discount and the acceptance run described above as the gating.

Cheers,

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few clarifying questions before we finalize language:

1) Production vs synthetic: during the acceptance run we prefer to use a masked subset of our production traces (we can redact PII). Can you confirm the harness will accept our trace format and that you will not persist raw inputs?
2) Peak bursts: how will short high-intensity bursts be treated? We understand sustained windows exclude bursts but need clarity for autoscaling cooldowns — what is your cooldown period and how does it affect the rolling window?
3) Credits & limits: the credit caps look reasonable — can you confirm whether credits reduce committed spend (i.e., are they credit notes) or are they applied as future invoice offsets?

If you can answer those three points and share the runbook and scripts we will move to legal for SOW insertion.

Ashley

Ashley — quick answers and next steps (this message will serve as the decision-log entry we discussed):

1) Trace handling: yes — the harness accepts common trace formats (JSON-lines, ndjson, or our replay CSV). We will provide a redaction guide; by default we do not persist raw inputs beyond the run logs (retained for 30 days) and will sign the mutual NDA addendum you requested. We will supply a sanitized CSV of per-request token counts if you prefer no content leaves your environment.

2) Bursts & autoscaling: autoscaling cooldown = 10 minutes by default. The stable-window calculation excludes windows where an autoscaling event occurred in that 30-minute interval. Short bursts that do not trigger autoscale are treated as part of workload variability and therefore count toward the sustained tokens/sec. We will document the exact detection heuristics in the runbook.

3) Credits: credits are issued as invoice offsets applied to the following billing cycle (i.e., future invoice credit). We will include the credit calculation logic in the SOW so it's auditable.

Next steps:
- We will upload the runbook, harness, and the acceptance checklist to the shared Drive folder by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed acceptance window: Tue 2026-08-17 02:00–05:00 PT (3h) — please confirm availability.
- Legal: Marissa will circulate the SOW clause with the Decision Log and commercial terms.

If that works I will mark this thread as the formal decision log entry and circulate a one-page SOW appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you into Dedicated.

Best,
Kimberly
